details:
The avatar scoring system has always been basic, and fairly arbitrary in what will dunk you straight to Very Poor (eg;  A Light).

My suggestion is to instead weight each check with a numerical score and aggregate it all to determine an Avatar's rank.

Eg;  Most stuff that'd go from Excellent to Very Poor (physbone count, for example) might have a weight of 1-4 depending on rank.  Larger performance impacts, eg a Light, might add a larger amount like 10 points.

Where it'd actually do some real good is the more dynamic values like Poly count and Texture Memory, mesh count, etc.  These would be accumulative based on size, so you might have, say, 50k-70k polys is 1 point per. (ie;  Excellent).  But when you start adding those up, you've got a trackable indicator of something that's blowing out due to a large model size but not necessarily other metrics.  Ditto for texture memory (say;  1 point per 50mb) as they ramp up.

This also means you have some flexibility in larger avatars, because you might have something with getting down to "just" Poor because you have some high-scoring checks but not others.

From all this your avatar scoring might look something like (Just for a broad example)

20 points == Excellent

50 points == Medium 

100+ points == Very Poor
title: Avatar Ranking should be an accumulative score, not binary checks
